program.title: How Line Graphs of Compound Growth Shape Retirement Investing Judgments
program.total_note: Totals are derived by summing the experiment-level Ns in the corrected thesis; the thesis does not print a single combined N.
program.population: Young adults who reported that they had not begun investing for retirement
program.core_manipulation: Presentation of identical retirement investment projections as line graphs versus numerical tables; Experiment 5 adds proportional area growth cards.

experiments.one_sentence: A standardized 40-year projection showed that presenting identical values as a line graph rather than a table substantially increased retirement-goal achievability.
experiments.objective: Initial test of whether presentation changes belief that adequate retirement wealth can be accumulated.
experiments.projection: Standardized 40-year projection; $100/month; 10% annual return with annual compounding; five-year display intervals.
experiments.next_step: Test whether the judgment effect extends to planned retirement contributions.

experiments.one_sentence: With projections personalized from current age to 65, line graphs increased both retirement-goal achievability and planned monthly retirement contributions.
experiments.objective: Test the downstream planned-contribution outcome and a statistical indirect effect through retirement-goal achievability.
experiments.projection: Personalized from current age to age 65; $100/month; 10% annual return with annual compounding.
experiments.next_step: Separate confidence in investment growth from confidence in personal ability to contribute.

experiments.one_sentence: Line graphs increased growth confidence, not ability confidence, providing process evidence that the display changed beliefs about what investment growth can accomplish rather than personal capacity to contribute.
experiments.objective: Distinguish growth confidence from ability confidence as potential pathways to retirement-goal achievability.
experiments.projection: Personalized from current age to age 65; same financial assumptions as Experiment 2.
experiments.next_step: Test whether line graphs change perceived compound-growth acceleration itself.

experiments.ultra_short_label: Does perceived acceleration help explain it?
experiments.one_sentence: Adding an Estimated Growth Ratio measure showed that line graphs increased perceived compound-growth acceleration and produced the strongest single-study evidence for the proposed statistical sequence through growth confidence and retirement-goal achievability.
experiments.objective: Directly assess perceived compound-growth acceleration and test the complete proposed statistical pathway.
experiments.projection: Personalized from current age to age 65; same financial assumptions; estimated-growth task added.
experiments.next_step: Test whether a connected trajectory is uniquely responsible or whether visual magnitude information is sufficient.

experiments.ultra_short_label: What part of the visual representation matters?
experiments.one_sentence: Adding proportional area growth cards replicated the line-graph-versus-table Estimated Growth Ratio difference but did not establish that the connected line trajectory was uniquely responsible.
experiments.objective: Probe connected-trajectory versus broader visual-magnitude explanations.
experiments.projection: Personalized from current age to age 65; identical projected values across all three conditions; area-card square areas proportional to values.
experiments.next_step: No sixth experiment in the thesis. The mechanism remains partially unresolved: connected trajectory and visual magnitude were not cleanly isolated.
